subject: bug in labs() need to use "colour", not "color"

messages.author: 07e91979a058d37c
messages.subject: bug in labs() need to use "colour", not "color"
parts:
I couldn't find where else to submit this, but I just wanted to write
this as a quick FYI that might save some one some time in the future.

I was struggling with two legends (one for shape, one for color) that
wouldn't merge together despite having the same names, breaks, labels,
etc. I fixed the problem by changing "color" to "colour" in the labs()
function.

Example:

data <- cars
data$group<-rep(LETTERS[1:2])

library(ggplot2)
ggplot(data, aes(x=speed,y=dist,color=group,shape=group)) +
geom_point() + labs(colour="Group",shape="Group")

produces a plot as expected with one legend. However,

data <- cars
data$group<-rep(LETTERS[1:2])

library(ggplot2)
ggplot(data, aes(x=speed,y=dist,color=group,shape=group)) +
geom_point() + labs(color="Group",shape="Group")

produces a plot with two legends and the legend for the color scale is
not relabeled. The only difference is the spelling of color (doesn't
work) vs colour (works) in naming the scales. This took me a bit of
time to track down (in a much more complicated piece of work); so I'm
posting it hoping it will save someone else time in the future.

Best wishes,
Scott
